evidence: The per-widget unconditional syncLayoutReaders() was quadratic per bulk commit (agent measured 97.5 ms vs master 48.0 ms at N=200), but the reviewer's headline mount case was identical on master (14159 vs 14304 ms at N=400). Rejecting microtask coalescing was right because it would reopen a stale-geometry window after each commit, which is the bug the PR removes.
guidance_note: Before replacing an O(1) per-widget call with a whole-registry walk inside a per-instance effect, benchmark a bulk commit at two sizes of N against master in the original PR.

evidence: 02d9a96 moved every caller to syncLayoutReadersForPass but left App.syncLayoutReaders/AppRuntime.syncLayoutReaders public with no caller, so the ungated quadratic walk stayed reachable. 32d9e97 made it private and deleted both delegators.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces a gated replacement for an API, grep the old name's callers in the same commit and delete or privatize the ungated version once it has no callers.

evidence: The 02d9a96 epoch gate means a sibling that registers after an earlier sibling has synced the pass never runs its reader in that commit. Before the fix every widget's effect swept the whole registry unconditionally. Only useWidget's second commit was masking the stale reader, and 32d9e97 fixed it by having registerLayoutReader run the reader.
guidance_note: When adding a once-per-epoch guard, list every fact the old unconditional call guaranteed (here: each newly registered reader measures in its own commit) and check that the guard still preserves each one.

evidence: The flag is a false positive for causation: the original 67a6097 comment already said 'one widget's commit can move any other widget's rectangle', so the sibling-displacement reliance and the missing test both predate 02d9a96. The added test passed on the existing design, so this was a real coverage gap rather than a bug.
guidance_note: When a design comment states the load-bearing claim (one widget's commit re-derives its siblings), write the test for that exact claim in the original PR.

evidence: The syncedLayoutPass = layoutPass assignment before the loop was introduced in 02d9a96 (the F1 fix), not in the flagged 32d9e97, which only made the method private. It turns one throwing reader into permanent staleness for the rest of the pass. The agent took the reviewer's first option (assign after the loop) and rightly declined the per-reader try/catch, which would have hidden failures.
guidance_note: When writing a 'work done' marker for a memoized sweep, set it after the sweep completes so the marker can never claim work that did not finish.

evidence: 02d9a96 added AppRuntime.syncLayoutReadersForPass/attachLayoutPassCounter, and App calls this.layoutEngine directly (app.tsx diff), so neither has a caller. The F2 fix deleted the same pattern under the old name only; the agent conceded 'I checked callers for the name I had just deleted rather than for the names I had just written.'
guidance_note: When a finding names a class of defect (an unused delegator added for symmetry), grep every method the PR added in that class, not just the one the finding names.

evidence: This duplicates F6 on the same lines: the AppRuntime delegators have no caller because App holds framework.layoutEngine directly and AppRuntime.layoutEngine is already a public readonly field. Both were deleted in 00a3bcb.
guidance_note: When a finding names a class of defect (an unused delegator added for symmetry), grep every method the PR added in that class, not just the one the finding names.

evidence: 32d9e97 (the F3 fix) added reader() after layoutReaders.set(). A reader that throws on first call therefore stays registered with no cleanup returned, and with the epoch it blocks every later sweep. Callers previously ran reader() before registering, and 00a3bcb restored that order.
guidance_note: When moving a call into a registration function, run the fallible step before mutating the registry so a throw leaves no half-registered entry.

narrative: The F1 epoch fix was a sound idea that spawned three fix-caused findings in round 1 and round 2: it left the ungated API public (F2), broke single-commit measurement for later siblings (F3), and marked passes synced before the sweep finished (F5). The F2 cleanup missed the same dead-delegator pattern under the new names (F6/F7), and the F3 fix introduced a set-before-call registration hazard (F8). Rounds 2 and 3 exist only because earlier fixes were incomplete; F4 was the only independent finding after round 0.
guidance_observations: Each fix was pushed after a full test run but without listing the invariants the replaced code had guaranteed, so every round found a guarantee the previous fix had silently dropped.
The agent's caller-sweep was keyed to the finding's literal symbol name instead of the defect class, which cost a whole round (F6/F7).

evidence: framework/index.ts exported MeasuredSizeReaderProps but src/index.ts omitted it, breaking the existing primitive-plus-props pattern. 1910db6 added it.
guidance_note: When adding a module to one barrel, diff its export list against every barrel that re-exports that module.

evidence: readdirSync recursive (Node 20.1) and Dirent.parentPath (20.12) are both above the declared engines >=18. 1910db6 replaced them with a manual recursive walk using only withFileTypes.
guidance_note: Before using a Node API in new code, check its introduction version against package.json engines.

evidence: The agent declined per-widget tests on the grounds that 'that regression can only originate at the seam', but the five consumers translate the value differently (Static renders unconstrained, Rule/Input draw nothing). F15 then found a consumer-level zero-width bug in Static that the seam-only test could not see.
guidance_note: When consumers each translate a shared discriminated value into different rendered behavior, test each consumer's rendered output and not only the seam's return value.

evidence: Duplicate of F2: recursive/parentPath are above the engines >=18 floor. Fixed by the same manual walk in 1910db6.
guidance_note: Before using a Node API in new code, check its introduction version against package.json engines.

evidence: The title 'is the only place the unmeasured case is decided' over-claimed what a four-literal regex checks. The reviewer offered narrowing as one option, and 1910db6 retitled the test to 'has not regrown any of the four fallbacks it replaced'.
guidance_note: Name a test for what its assertion actually checks, not for the invariant you hope it implies.

evidence: Both test files were grep-based or settling checks, and none mounted a widget to assert undefined vs 0. measured-size-reader.test.tsx added both arms; building it showed the WidgetHost path has no unmeasured window, which confirms the gap was real.
guidance_note: When a PR's whole purpose is a runtime distinction, write a test that mounts the code and observes both arms before adding structural grep guards.

evidence: resolveVisualRenderWidth(0) changed from undefined to 1 on an exported function. Aligning the behavior (floor 0) instead of documenting the wart was a defensible choice. However, the agent's own note that normalizeVisualWidth re-floors to 1 downstream marked the end-to-end path as unverified, and that path regressed (F15).
guidance_note: When changing a function's output at a boundary value, follow that value through every downstream consumer to the rendered frame before pushing.

evidence: Third report of the same Node-version gap (parentPath undefined on Node 18). Fixed by the manual walk in 1910db6.
guidance_note: Before using a Node API in new code, check its introduction version against package.json engines.

evidence: The grep-over-comments cost was real (the rule-component comment had to be reworded). However, the boundary check was the ticket's named acceptance criterion, and the repo has no ESLint config to host an AST rule. The agent narrowed the over-claiming title, added runtime tests, and kept the grep.

No test drove a real zero-width placement. The fix asserts the seam reports {0,0} for display:none, but the reviewer also asked for rendered output reflecting zero room. Asserting only the seam value is why Static's broken zero rendering survived until F15.
guidance_note: When a reviewer asks for an end-to-end assertion on rendered output, assert the frame, not an intermediate value.

evidence: The agent changed the floor to 0 but declined having Static skip rendering at 0, claiming that 'would need normalizeVisualWidth to stop flooring to 1'. 2e23d1d later did exactly the reviewer's suggestion (renderWidth === 0 ? null) without touching normalizeVisualWidth. The half-fix made the output worse (14 rows vs master's 8).
guidance_note: Before declining part of a suggested fix as out of scope, try the suggestion as written; here the consumer-side null check needed no downstream change.

evidence: The agent reports running Content.fromText("hello").truncate(0, {overflow: "ellipsis"}).plain and getting "", but rich-js's truncate implementation is not in the packet, so zero-safety rests on that reported run. The 1910db6 change also narrows the path so only a real measurement reaches truncate.

measureElement returns yogaNode.getComputedWidth(), and Yoga bounds resolved dimensions at non-negative values; negative margins move origin, not size. The reviewer hedged ('could not fully rule this out'). A clamp would silence an engine contract violation, and the RangeError is the louder failure.

With width undefined on the unmeasured pass, availableWidth fell back to label.cellLength, so a long border title could overflow and stretch the box being measured. Restoring the CSS-first read would reintroduce a second width source, which F16's width:5/min-width:16 case shows diverges. Skipping the label when unmeasured is the tighter fix.
guidance_note: When an input can be 'unknown', decide for each consumer what it renders in that state instead of substituting the content's natural size.

evidence: 1910db6's Math.max(0, ...) let a real 0 reach normalizeVisualWidth, which floors to 1. The agent measured 14 interleaved rows against master's 8, so the fix made the zero case worse. The reviewer asked only to pin the behavior; the agent instead fixed it (Static renders null at 0) and pinned that, which is the better call.
guidance_note: When changing a function's output at a boundary value, follow that value through every downstream consumer to the rendered frame before pushing.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the dropped cssWidth fallback in sparkline-component.tsx dates from the original commit, while 2e23d1d touched only visual.tsx, static-component.tsx and a test. The agent's frame dumps show frame 0 is empty under both variants, so the 'statically known' CSS width was not known yet, and the CSS-first read renders 5 cols permanently where width:5/min-width:16 resolves to 16. The real frame-1 flash was filed as its own ticket and the min-width case pinned in a test.

narrative: Round 0 raised 14 findings, mostly test-coverage and Node-compat gaps, handled cleanly in one commit. The one costly misstep was F11: the agent changed resolveVisualRenderWidth's floor to 0 but wrongly declined the consumer-side 'render nothing' half, which made Static's zero-width output worse than master and cost round 1 (F15). F16 was a reviewer premise built on a false first-frame assumption that the agent disproved with frame dumps and a pinning test.
guidance_observations: The agent tested the seam's return value but not consumers' rendered output (F3, F10), and the bug the reviewer warned about appeared exactly in a consumer.
Measuring against master and dumping frames before answering (F15, F16) consistently produced the right call; reasoning about scope without running the suggestion (F11) produced the wrong one.

evidence: postToFocused carries Paste/Click/Mouse*/Resize, and only Key sets handlesKeyBindings, so the empty-chain route silently dropped every non-key message when nothing was focused. 22a70b9 took the reviewer's split option: postKey has its own focus-only route, and the old chain is restored as resolveFallbackDeliveryTarget. The added paste/resize tests fail against the flagged commit.
guidance_note: Before changing what a shared resolver returns, list every caller and every message type routed through it, and confirm each still has a delivery path.

evidence: dispatchMessage returns early on undefined, and the PR changed undefined from 'no interactive widgets' to 'nothing focused', so App.dispatchMessage silently stopped delivering. Instead of adding no-focus handling as the reviewer suggested, the agent withdrew the regression by restoring the old chain for this caller, which is the smaller and truer fix.
guidance_note: Before changing what a shared resolver returns, list every caller and every message type routed through it, and confirm each still has a delivery path.

evidence: Same defect as F1: non-Key messages posted with no focus enter the queue and are discarded because handlesKeyBindings is Key-only. Fixed by the same split in 22a70b9, with regression tests.
guidance_note: Before changing what a shared resolver returns, list every caller and every message type routed through it, and confirm each still has a delivery path.

evidence: AppLifecycle.postResize goes through postToFocused, so every unfocused terminal resize dropped Resize handlers. The restored fallback chain covers it, and a postResize(120, 40) test yields [] on the flagged commit and ['120x40'] after.
guidance_note: Before changing what a shared resolver returns, list every caller and every message type routed through it, and confirm each still has a delivery path.

narrative: The PR narrowed a shared focus resolver to fix key routing, and in doing so broke every other caller of that resolver (paste, mouse, resize, dispatchMessage). The reviewer found all of them in round 0. One fix that split key routing from fallback delivery resolved all four, and round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: The agent admitted seeing the dispatchMessage guard and 'talking myself past it'; a caller enumeration of the changed resolver before the first push would have kept the PR to a single round.

evidence: normalizeKeyList split on commas without trimming and relied on normalizeKeyName's trim to drop whitespace segments, so keeping ' ' bound the space bar ('f7, ' binds save to space). e56b5c2 moved trimming into the list grammar and removed it from normalizeKeyName. The new test fails on 27845b4 with expected ['save'] to equal [].
guidance_note: When changing a shared normalizer's handling of an input, grep its callers for any that relied on the old behavior (here, the list parser relying on trim to drop padding).

narrative: There was a single finding: a space-bar fix in a shared key normalizer silently changed how a second grammar (comma-separated keymaps) handled padding. The agent fixed it by moving trimming to the grammar that has padding and pinned both directions with tests. Round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: Same shape as textual-js#7: a shared function changed for one caller without enumerating the others.

evidence: content.ts:419 routes an omitted markup option through fromMarkup, so footerGlyphs parsed chip text as markup. However, the reviewer's examples ('Save [Ctrl+S]', '[') pass through unchanged; only recognized tags like '[b]' diverge. The fix ({markup: false}) was right, and the agent built the test on 'Toggle [b]old' so it actually fails pre-fix.
guidance_note: When moving display text from plain Text into a markup-capable builder, pass markup:false explicitly at the helper.

evidence: strip-ansi was imported by tests but absent from package.json, so it resolved only through hoisting from ../rich-js. 77ecb40 added it to devDependencies but did not regenerate the lockfile (see F4).
guidance_note: Add a dependency with npm install so package.json and the lockfile change together, then confirm with npm ci.

evidence: The reviewer's own parity target, footer_with_bindings.json, records cells 0 and 2 (the padding spaces) as fg=#ffa62b bold=True, so the merged styled run matches Python and the old split diverged. Both footers compare at AE == 0.
77ecb40 edited package.json alone, leaving packages[""].devDependencies in package-lock.json without strip-ansi, so npm ci would fail. ae0539a regenerated the lockfile and verified with npm ci.
guidance_note: Add a dependency with npm install so package.json and the lockfile change together, then confirm with npm ci.

narrative: Round 0 raised three findings: a real markup-parsing bug (examples overstated), a real undeclared test dependency, and an inverted styling claim that the agent refuted from the Python snapshot. The dependency fix hand-edited package.json without regenerating the lockfile, which cost round 1 entirely.
guidance_observations: Hand-editing a manifest instead of using the package manager left the lockfile out of sync and cost a full review round.

evidence: The agent confirmed <Text width={a > b ? 1 : 2} color="red"> escapes [^>]*?. Banning the Text import in src/widgets removes the need for tag parsing, and it flagged both pre-PR offenders. The claim that this made the class 'unrepresentable' was too strong, as F5 showed.
guidance_note: When replacing a pattern check with a capability ban, enumerate every syntactic way to obtain the capability (named, namespace, default+namespace imports) before claiming the class is closed.

evidence: The reviewer's proposed Math.round was wrong: Bar._validate_percentage uses int(), and the agent's real-Textual values (53 -> 33/64) match Math.trunc. The comment did say 'rounding' and nothing pinned non-lattice percentages, so the agent kept the code, fixed the comment, and added 53/33/99% tests.
guidance_note: When porting a quantization step, write the comment with the exact operation of the source (int() truncates) and pin at least one off-lattice value from the reference implementation.

evidence: setdefault leaves a shell-exported TEXTUAL_ANIMATIONS in place while render-fixture-xvfb.sh forces none, which reopens the JSON/PNG frame divergence the comment describes. f2bf713 assigns it unconditionally.
guidance_note: When two capture paths must agree on a setting, set it unconditionally in both rather than defaulting it in one.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: renderBar dates from the original commit, and f2bf713 did not touch bar-renderable.ts. The 11-glyph arithmetic is right, but real Textual overruns identically, so 'fixing' it would diverge from the reference. The agent corrected the docstring and pinned the Python output, including the sharper rule 'empty after snapping'.
guidance_note: When porting a renderable, write its docstring from the reference implementation's actual edge behavior instead of the idealized contract.

evidence: The f2bf713 ink-text-import regex matches only import { ... Text ... }, so import * as Ink still reaches <Ink.Text>, contradicting the fix's own 'unrepresentable' claim. dd1836c added a module-blind namespace-import ban, mirroring check-framework-imports.
guidance_note: When replacing a pattern check with a capability ban, enumerate every syntactic way to obtain the capability (named, namespace, default+namespace imports) before claiming the class is closed.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the Sparkline Text-to-renderContent swap was in the original commit, and f2bf713 did not touch sparkline-component.tsx, so the missing component test predates review. The added truecolour test fails against the pre-PR Text rendering, so it pins the real defect.
guidance_note: When the same rendering change is applied to two widgets, add the same frame-level tests to both in the original PR.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: dd1836c did not touch INDETERMINATE_RANGE or highlightRange, which date from before review. The existing indeterminate tests checked only '--%' and the class. The new frame test fails against the originally shipped [0, 0.2] range.
guidance_note: When a value was once wrong and only a pixel gate caught it, add a unit-level frame assertion for it in the same commit as the correction.

evidence: The dd1836c regex /import\s*\*\s*as/ cannot skip a default binding, so import Default, * as Ink from "ink" passed both rules. 3351554 widened it and checked it against both spellings.
guidance_note: When replacing a pattern check with a capability ban, enumerate every syntactic way to obtain the capability (named, namespace, default+namespace imports) before claiming the class is closed.

narrative: The lint-rule hardening took three rounds of one-spelling-at-a-time patches: a tag regex, then a named-import ban, then a namespace ban, then default+namespace. Each fix claimed the class was closed and the next round found another import form. The rounds were not strictly avoidable because each also carried independent test-gap findings (F4, F6, F7). The agent's pushbacks on quantization (F2) and bar overrun (F4) were verified against real Textual and were right.
guidance_observations: Enumerating the ES import grammar once (named, namespace, default+namespace) at the F1 fix would have closed the F5 and F8 findings in a single commit.

Test gaps for unchanged pre-review code (Sparkline frame, indeterminate frame) surfaced only across later rounds; a coverage pass over every behavior the PR changed, done before the first push, would have caught them together.
